# A missing emission stage or a stale corpus must fail the run

Refs #17920

## Context

Delivery leaf of #17920. That ticket carries six ACs across two sides of a repository boundary; this one owns exactly the two that are **Engine-side, mechanically verifiable, and deliverable in one PR** — the guards that make the outage loud. Its remaining four (Brain-side emission ownership, the watchdog alarm-body correction, and the two post-merge scheduled-run observations) stay with the parent.

Filed at @neo-gpt-emmy's RA-3 on PR #17927, whose corrected framing is right and which I initially argued against: a leaf for the slice a PR actually delivers is **delivery decomposition**, not a ticket opened to satisfy a body linter. The same shape is live in this repo twice today — #17924 under #17922, and #17931 under #17921.

`c623b2f63c` removed the `GitHub Workflow corpus` emission stage from `emissionCommands`. The pipeline went **shorter, not red**: two stages, both green, `no-generated-changes`, exit 0, for five days — while the surviving derivation stage kept rebuilding the portal from a corpus frozen on 2026-08-26 and committing the result. The full account of how that happened, who it hurt, and why the stage cannot simply be restored in place is in #17920 and is not repeated here.

## The Problem

Two independent silences, one outage.

**1. A vanished producer reads as a shorter run.** `emissionCommands` is a table; the pipeline executes whatever is in it. Nothing anywhere states which stages are *expected*, so removing an entry cannot fail — there is no expectation to violate. `no-generated-changes` is reachable by **having no generator**, and that is indistinguishable from "nothing changed upstream".

**2. Derivation consumes whatever age the corpus happens to be.** `content indexes and SEO` reads `resources/content/{issues,pulls,discussions}` and writes the portal's chunked indexes, id maps and crawler manifests. It has no opinion about how old that input is, so a frozen corpus produces fresh derived commits on schedule. Anyone reading run status or commit recency concludes the pipeline is healthy — the derived commits are the *evidence* of health, and they are exactly what the defect manufactures.

The two guards are separate because the failures are: (1) sees an Engine-side table shrink, (2) sees an **absent producer** that never appears in that table at all, because the emitter is Agent-OS-side. Neither subsumes the other.

## The Architectural Reality

- `buildScripts/dataSyncPipeline.mjs` — `emissionCommands` (the stage table) and the derivation stage that reads the corpus. Both guards land here, as assertions that run **before** the work they gate.
- `buildScripts/dataSyncWatchdog.mjs` — owns the corpus-age policy. Its resolver is the single site the guard must read through; a guard that imports the default constant while the alarm resolves the `WATCHDOG_MAX_CORPUS_AGE_HOURS` override does not share policy with it, it merely shares a number. That divergence was real and is what makes "one effective policy owner" part of this leaf rather than an afterthought.
- Corpus freshness must be read from **committed** dates (`git log -1 --format=%cI`), never `mtime`: this runs in an ephemeral Actions checkout where every file's mtime is checkout time, so an mtime probe certifies a five-day-old corpus as seconds fresh.
- ADR 0040 §2.3 fixes the direction — the Agent OS consumes the published Engine and is never imported by it. Every guard in this leaf is Engine-side only and adds no `neo-agent-brain` dependency. **Locator:** ADR 0040 is not in this repository; it lives at `neo-agent-brain:learn/agentos/decisions/0040-agentos-extraction-topology.md` §2.3, and grepping `learn/agentos/decisions/` here returns nothing because it is the wrong tree, not because the citation is wrong.

## The Fix

1. **A stage-set assertion.** The pipeline asserts the emission stages it expects **before any stage executes** — so a pipeline that lost a generator cannot first publish what the survivors derive and only then mention the gap. That derived commit is the thing that made the outage read as healthy. The expectation is declared as an **independent literal**, not derived from the table it checks: a witness derived from the thing it witnesses attests to nothing.
2. **A corpus-freshness guard.** Derivation refuses a corpus older than the effective corpus-age band, naming every stale facet with its measured age. A facet with no visible commit resolves to stale, not to "no age to compare" — that direction fails closed.
3. **One effective policy owner.** Both the guard and the watchdog alarm resolve the band through a single resolution site, **per call** rather than through an imported constant, so an override set after module load is honoured and the two cannot disagree about the same corpus.

## Contract Ledger Matrix

| Target Surface | Source of Authority | Behavior | Fallback | Docs | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `emissionCommands` stage set | this ticket (delegated from #17920) | asserted by label before execution; a missing expected stage fails the run | none — `no-generated-changes` must be unreachable by having no generator | `dataSyncPipeline.mjs` JSDoc | negative control: delete a stage entry, the run must go red and every unrelated arm must stay green |
| `content indexes and SEO` input | this ticket (delegated from #17920) | refuses to derive from a corpus older than the effective corpus-age band | none — deriving from stale input is the defect | stage JSDoc | negative control: age the corpus past the band, the stage must not report success |
| corpus-age **policy** | `dataSyncWatchdog.mjs` | one resolution site, resolved per call by every consumer; the constant is never the policy | none | `dataSyncWatchdog.mjs` JSDoc | negative control: set `WATCHDOG_MAX_CORPUS_AGE_HOURS`, assert guard and alarm agree about one corpus at one moment |
| freshness measurement | this ticket | committed dates via `git log`, never `mtime` | absent commit ⇒ stale | stage JSDoc | an mtime-based probe must be shown to certify a known-stale corpus as fresh |

## Decision Record impact

`aligned-with ADR 0040` — §2.3 is why both guards are Engine-side and why the producer's absence is detectable only on the corpus-age axis. No ADR is amended.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A negative control proves the stage-set assertion: removing an expected entry from `emissionCommands` turns the run **red**, shown failing against the pre-guard implementation first — today it turns the run *shorter*.
- [ ] The assertion runs before any stage executes, so a run that lost a generator publishes nothing derived before failing.
- [ ] The expected stage set is an independent literal; a mutation that derives it from `emissionCommands` must be shown to make the witness vacuous.
- [ ] A negative control proves the freshness guard: with the corpus aged past the effective band, the derivation stage does not report success and names each stale facet with its measured age.
- [ ] Guard and watchdog alarm resolve one effective band through a single site: with `WATCHDOG_MAX_CORPUS_AGE_HOURS` set, an arm that passes **no** explicit threshold reds against a re-imported-constant mutation and nothing else. An arm that passes an explicit threshold is not sufficient — it stays green against the defect.
- [ ] Freshness is measured from committed dates; a facet with no visible commit is treated as stale.
- [ ] No Engine-side code imports or spawns Brain substrate; `package.json` gains no `neo-agent-brain` dependency. `check-engine-brain-boundary` exit 0.

## Out of Scope

- **Restoring GitHub corpus emission itself** (#17920 AC-1). The producer is Agent-OS-side; this leaf makes its absence loud, it does not fill the hole.
- **The `#17834` alarm body** still asserting "runs fail on schedule" against a zero streak (#17920 AC-5).
- **The two post-merge scheduled-run observations** (#17920 AC-6) — they need wall-clock runs, not a merge.
- **Collapsing or re-designing the watchdog's two axes.** The corpus-age axis is the only thing that caught this; the axes stay separate.
- **A tighter band than 48h.** That needs a producer heartbeat proving the corpus *current* rather than merely *recently changed*, and that producer is in the other repository.

## Avoided Traps

- **Deriving the expected stage set from `emissionCommands`.** It reads as DRY and is the one thing that makes the guard vacuous. The credential vocabulary in the same file is rightly centralized — there, drift *is* the defect; here, drift *is the signal*.
- **`mtime` for freshness.** Cheap, obvious, and certifies the exact five-day-old corpus this ticket exists for as seconds fresh, because the Actions checkout stamps every file.
- **Treating an unmeasurable facet as fresh.** Failing open on the measurement is the same class of silence as the outage.
- **Sharing a default and calling it shared policy.** A constant and a resolver agree right up until an override exists, which is precisely when the answer matters.
